- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to drop; if below, tends to rise — adjust for 1–2% lagged momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent sentiment; if sentiment peaks early, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment history shows high volatility (e.g., alternating 0.1–0.5), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
